title: On-Prem Telemetry Sampling, Privacy, and Cost Control Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
  ========
  This playbook defines recommended telemetry sampling, privacy-preserving practices, and cost-control mechanisms for Redwood Inference private (VPC / on‑prem) deployments. It is intended for platform engineers and customer-facing delivery teams responsible for installing and operating the Redwood control plane and runtime in customer networks.

  Goals
  -----
  - Provide a repeatable sampling policy that preserves signal for debugging and model-quality monitoring while limiting site-to-cloud bandwidth and storage costs.
  - Describe mandatory privacy and PII minimization steps that must be applied before any telemetry leaves a customer boundary.
  - Provide knobs for cost throttling, retention limits, and alerting to keep observability spend predictable.

  Scope
  -----
  Applies to: on‑prem and VPC Private deployments where telemetry is transported from the customer environment to Redwood’s optional control plane or a customer-managed observability endpoint. Does not replace customer contractual obligations; security/legal teams must approve when sending telemetry off‑prem.

  Principles
  ----------
  - Minimize: never send full user prompts, credentials, or full PII unless explicitly approved and encrypted.
  - Sample with intent: sample at higher rates for error traces and model-quality signals; lower rates for routine metrics and high-volume traces.
  - Cost-aware defaults: deployments ship with conservative defaults that limit retention and ingest volume; operators can opt-in to higher fidelity.
  - Auditable transformations: any redaction/anonymization must be reversible only by the customer (when required) and recorded in the deployment audit log.

  Required Roles & Ownership
  --------------------------
  - Delivery Engineer (owner): implements sampling policy during install and documents deviations.
  - Customer Security Contact: approves any telemetry leaving their network; signs off on PII policy.
  - Observability Team (Redwood): validates ingestion configuration and enforces cost guardrails for hosted ingest.

  Sampling strategy
  -----------------
  1) Categories and default sample rates (recommended defaults):
     - Error traces (runtime exceptions, OOM, model-inference failures): 100% (capture all)
     - Slow requests (latency > 95th percentile threshold): 100% for first 1k per day, then 10%
     - Model-quality signals (evaluations, labelled prompts): 25%
     - Token-level metrics (per-token timings and GPU counters): 1–5% (configurable)
     - Audit logs (authN/authZ changes): 100% for 90 days, then 0%

  2) Adaptive sampling
     - Implement reservoir sampling for high-volume trace spans: keep a fixed-size reservoir per minute (default 100 spans/min).
     - Use priority sampling for traces containing new error signatures or model regression flags: override to 100% for the first 24h after detection.

  3) Edge-side aggregation
     - Aggregate counters and histograms at the agent before export (percentiles, counts, sums) to reduce cardinality and payload size.
     - Emit summarized metrics every 30s by default; high-resolution (5s) only for explicitly whitelisted debug sessions.

  Privacy and PII handling
  ------------------------
  All telemetry that could contain user data must be processed using the following pipeline before leaving the customer boundary.

  1) Redaction & token masking
     - Replace user prompts and freeform text with tokenized hash placeholders by default: prompt_hash = HMAC_SHA256(prompt, customer_kms_key_id).
     - Retain only model-level metadata (model_id, model_version, latency, token_counts) in cleartext.

  2) Deterministic hashing rules
     - For deduplication and root-cause workflows, use deterministic HMAC with the customer's KMS key. Do not store raw PII anywhere in Redwood-managed storage.

  3) Differential privacy options (optional)
     - For deployments processing sensitive datasets, enable local DP noise on counts before export (Laplace mechanism with epsilon configured per-customer).

  4) Encryption in transit and at rest
     - All exports must use TLS1.2+ with mutual TLS (mTLS) when sending to Redwood-managed endpoints.
     - At-rest encryption MUST be provided by the customer for any telemetry stored within customer-managed buckets; Redwood-managed storage for private telemetry requires a customer-supplied envelope key.

  Retention, storage tiers, and cost controls
  -------------------------------------------
  Recommended retention tiers (configurable per-customer):

  | Tier         | Default retention | Purpose                                    |
  |--------------|-------------------|--------------------------------------------|
  | Hot          | 7 days            | Immediate troubleshooting and SLOs         |
  | Warm         | 30 days           | Quality regressions & short-term audits    |
  | Cold/Archive | 365 days (opt-in) | Long-term compliance (customer managed)    |

  Cost guardrails
  - Monthly ingest cap: default 200 GB/month per deployment. Exceeding cap disables non-critical telemetry exports until approved by customer security contact.
  - Per-ingest rate limiting: token-level export limited to 10 MB/s by default; bursts allowed up to 2x for 60s.
  - Alert thresholds:
    - 80% of monthly cap: email + Slack notify to Delivery Engineer and customer security contact.
    - 95% of monthly cap: automatic sampling reduction to minimal mode and PagerDuty page.

  Operational runbook
  -------------------
  Incident: Unexpected high telemetry volume
  1) Triage (0–15m)
     - Verify inbound throughput on local agent: ssh to telemetry-agent host and run `telemetryctl stats`.
     - Check sampling policy: `telemetryctl config show | grep sample_rate`.
 2) Containment (15–60m)
     - Flip deployment to minimal sampling: `telemetryctl set --sampling-mode minimal`.
     - If sending to Redwood-hosted ingest, temporarily revoke exporter token from control plane and notify Redwood SRE.
 3) Root cause & restore (1–24h)
     - Pull last 24h aggregated histograms and run cardinality analysis to find new high-cardinality keys.
     - Re-enable selective high-fidelity samples only for owners of affected service.

  Incident: Suspected PII leakage
  1) Immediate actions
     - Stop all telemetry export: `telemetryctl set --export enabled=false`.
     - Snapshot local agent config and logs; store encrypted copy for audit.
 2) Investigation
     - Run content-scan tool with redaction rules to find leaked fields: `redwood-scan --rules pii-standard-v1 /var/log/telemetry`.
 3) Remediation
     - Apply stricter redaction rules and rotate exporter credentials. Re-run tests to validate no raw data leaves the environment.

  Configuration examples
  ----------------------
  Example sampling config (YAML)

  ```yaml
  telemetry:
    sampling:
      error_traces: 1.0
      slow_requests: 0.1
      model_quality: 0.25
      token_metrics: 0.02
    reservoir:
      spans_per_minute: 100
    aggregation:
      histogram_precision: 0.01
      summary_interval_seconds: 30
  export:
    endpoint: https://observability.redwood.example
    tls:
      mode: mTLS
      client_cert_path: /etc/telemetry/client.pem
    encryption:
      envelope_key_kms_id: projects/..../keys/..../
  cost_control:
    monthly_ingest_cap_gb: 200
    burst_multiplier: 2
  ```

  Example redaction pseudocode
  ```
  function redact_prompt(prompt, kms_key_id):
      # deterministic HMAC using customer key
      return HMAC_SHA256(prompt, kms_key_id)
  ```

  Acceptance tests & verification
  ------------------------------
  - After install, run the post-install telemetry checklist (see related page) and confirm:
    - No raw prompt text is present in exported payloads.
    - mTLS handshake completes and exporter certificate is validated against Redwood's CA bundle.
    - Monthly ingest estimate reported by agent does not exceed configured cap.

  Rollout checklist (Delivery Engineer)
  ------------------------------------
  1) Confirm customer telemetry policy and sign-off.
  2) Configure sampling YAML and ship a template under /etc/telemetry/config.yaml.
  3) Provide a KMS key identifier and validate HMAC-based hashing locally.
  4) Run acceptance tests and capture results in the deployment ticket.
  5) Enable 7-day hot retention and confirm alerting integrations.

  Metrics and SLOs
  ----------------
  - Telemetry export uptime SLO: 99.9% (monthly).
  - Detection latency for error traces: < 30s from event to export (hot path).
  - False positive PII detection rate in automated scans: < 1%

  FAQs
  ----
  Q: What if the customer forbids any data egress?
  A: Redwood supports fully customer-managed observability where telemetry is written to a customer S3/GCS bucket or a self-hosted Grafana/Prometheus stack. In that case, follow the same sampling and redaction rules locally and do not export to Redwood-hosted endpoints.

  Q: Can customers opt out of hashing to enable human-readable debugging?
  A: Only with explicit signed approval and a temporary window; do not store raw data in Redwood-managed systems.

  Appendix
  -------
  - Diagnostic commands
    - telemetryctl stats
    - telemetryctl config show
    - redwood-scan --rules pii-standard-v1

  - Reference: see hardware telemetry spec and day‑2 post installation checklist in related pages for integration steps and expected agent versions.

  End of document
